chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Imran who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Should I shorten the prayer in the Sacred Mosque or complete it? He said, 'If you shorten it, it is good; and if you complete it, it is better, and the addition of goodness is good.'

key_terms.إِقْصَار: Shortening the prayer (performing two rak'ahs instead of four)

ai.seo_question: Should one shorten or complete the four-rak'ah prayer when praying in the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for the traveler praying in the Sacred Mosque, affirming that while shortening the prayer is valid, completing it is superior as it constitutes an act of extra devotion (ziyadah al-khayr). This reflects the Shia scholarly preference for completing prayers in the three sacred mosques (Mecca, Medina, Jerusalem) even for travelers, distinguishing it from the general rule of shortening. The Imam’s response highlights the principle that voluntary acts of worship in sacred spaces carry enhanced spiritual merit.
